title: Chronicle: compact interaction mode for high-density time-series with screen reader summaries
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a compact interaction mode for the 'Chronicle' time-series component that gracefully degrades visual density and surfaces concise, consumable summaries to screen reader users. Goals: 1) reduce visual clutter for >500 series/point views using adaptive sampling and token-driven styling; 2) provide a keyboard-first summary experience that announces range aggregates (min/median/max, notable anomalies) without overwhelming aria channels; 3) keep performance budget under 12ms additional frame cost on typical dashboards by using precomputed rolling aggregates and off-main-thread summarization. This ticket covers design patterns, token updates, and handoff artifacts for engineering implementation.

design_decisions: Use a single summarizer component that renders both visual 'summary chip' and accessible announcement to keep copy consistent.
Three density tiers (full, condensed, compact) driven by a new chart token 'chart.density' that maps to sampling/decimation strategy.
Announce only on explicit user action (keyboard toggle or confirmed range selection), not on hover, to limit screen reader noise.
Precompute rolling aggregates on ingestion where available; otherwise compute lightweight aggregates in a WebWorker and cache results per chart session.
Keep short summary <=160 chars, medium <=320 chars; verbose reserved for detailed shareable report (out of scope for this ticket).

notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Aggressive server-side precomputation reduces client CPU but increases storage/ingestion complexity; 2) Client-side summarization keeps data private and reduces infra changes but increases browser CPU and power on low-end devices. Decided on hybrid approach. Performance guardrails: CPU work above 12ms/frame must be offloaded and summarized results cached for the session.
